title: Completion of a local ring with finite-dimensional special fibre is finite over the completion of the base
statement: Let $\varphi:(R,\mathfrak m)\to(S,\mathfrak n)$ be a local homomorphism of local rings ($\varphi(\mathfrak m)\subseteq\mathfrak n$) such that the ideals $\mathfrak m$ and $\mathfrak n$ are finitely generated and $S/\mathfrak mS$ is a finite-dimensional vector space over $\kappa=R/\mathfrak m$, where $\mathfrak m^kS$ denotes the ideal of $S$ generated by $\varphi(\mathfrak m^k)$. Let $R^\wedge=\varprojlim_kR/\mathfrak m^k$ and $S^\wedge=\varprojlim_kS/\mathfrak n^k$ be the $\mathfrak m$-adic and $\mathfrak n$-adic completions [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and $\varphi^\wedge:R^\wedge\to S^\wedge$ the ring map $(r_k\bmod\mathfrak m^k)_k\mapsto(\varphi(r_k)\bmod\mathfrak n^k)_k$ (well defined since $\varphi(\mathfrak m^k)\subseteq\mathfrak n^k$). Let $S'=\varprojlim_kS/\mathfrak m^kS$ be the $\mathfrak m$-adic completion of $S$; since $\mathfrak m^kS\subseteq\mathfrak n^k$ the quotient maps $S/\mathfrak m^kS\to S/\mathfrak n^k$ induce a ring map $\gamma:S'\to S^\wedge$. Then (1) $\gamma$ is an isomorphism, i.e. $S^\wedge$ is the $\mathfrak m$-adic completion of $S$; and (2) $S^\wedge$, an $R^\wedge$-module via $\varphi^\wedge$, is a finitely generated $R^\wedge$-module.
